title: MAGTF Officer Instructor (II/III) (LtCol to 1stLt) and (CWO5 to WO) EMOS (0202, 0302, 0402, 0430, 0602, 0802, 1302, 2602, 3002, 3102, 3510, 5902, 6002, 6802, 7002, 7202, 7204, 7208, 7210, 7220, 7315), CG TECOM
raw_text:
11. MOS 0982, MAGTF Officer Instructor (II/III) (LtCol to 1stLt) and (CWO5
to WO) EMOS (0202, 0302, 0402, 0430, 0602, 0802, 1302, 2602, 3002, 3102,
3510, 5902, 6002, 6802, 7002, 7202, 7204, 7208, 7210, 7220, 7315), CG TECOM

    a. Summary. Marine Officers assigned to a teaching billet or faculty
position that facilitate learning as their primary duty who teaches a
designated course approved by the appropriate general/flag officer in the
chain of command. Augmented personnel support used as training aids (e.g.
role players and/or demonstrator cadre) for instruction are not categorized
to be an instructor.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Fully qualified in the primary MOS aligned with the instructor
billet.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Completion of the locally executed, TECOM approved, service-level
instructor course(s) or other service instructor course.

        (2) EMOS approval authority is only by O-6 level commanding officer/
director under MAGTFTC.

            (3) Serve in a specified MAGTF instructor designated billet.

        (4) Serve as MAGTF Instructor for one-year, however, and this is
waiverable only by O-6 level commanding/director under MAGTFTC.

        (5) CG, MAGTFTC will be the approving authority for all waivers where
Marines are not currently assigned to fill a designated Instructor billet BIC
or any other request which does not meet the requirements listed above.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Facilitate student-centered, active-learning experiences in order
to achieve learning objectives and associated learning outcomes using
specific curriculum, instructional strategies, and teaching methods/
methodologies appropriate to the learning program as necessary to meet
service defined occupational learning requirements.

        (2) Creatively facilitate learning activities and reflective events
based on current and emerging research and approved local lesson files.
Continue personal and professional development to improve performance and
support the enterprise-level changes needed to develop and expand critical-
thinking in our service members.




                                          1-66                       Enclosure (1)
 1111                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Participate in various committees, course content/learning
experience review boards (CCRBs/CLERBs), curriculum review boards (CRBs), and
working groups that deal with learning matters and academic policy issues, in
order to advance curriculum standards and encourage facilitator proficiency.

        (4) Provide input into the decision-making and policy-making aspects
of the facilitating, assessing, designing, and enabling learning faculty
development continuums.

        (5) Collaborate with learning design/curriculum development staff to
design and develop active, student-centered learning experiences.

        (6) Facilitate various student-centered methods including,
discussions, decision-forcing scenarios, decision games, coaching, and
mentoring with an emphasis on combining a practiced speed and accuracy with
the known to solve unknown problems which exercise creativity, judgment, and
critical thinking. Collaboratively generate constructive feedback with
learners and with other facilitators as they employ these methods.

        (7) Mentor and coach students regarding their academic progress,
learning, and professional development.

        (8) Create opportunities for students to collaborate and share their
own professional and academic experiences to enhance student learning and
nurture an open, safe environment in which meaningful discussions can thrive.

        (9) Arrange conferences and guest speakers, plan staff rides, and
update information in MCTIMS, employ MarineNet’s E-Learning Ecosystem (to
include Moodle), and leverage other applicable learning capabilities.

        (10) Guide learning through measurable learning objectives and
student-centered, active-learning outcomes, assess students’ achievement of
those learning objectives/learning outcomes, and support continual process
improvement of curricula based on the assessment results.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
